title: Convergence of Sharpness-Aware Minimization Algorithms using Increasing Batch Size and Decaying Learning Rate
main_claims: GSAM with an increasing batch size achieves epsilon-approximation convergence to the approximated SAM problem with provable convergence guarantees.
GSAM with a decaying learning rate (cosine annealing or linear) also achieves epsilon-approximation convergence.
Using an increasing batch size or decaying learning rate empirically finds flatter local minima than using constant batch size and learning rate.
methodology: The authors prove convergence theorems for the GSAM algorithm (gap-guided SAM) under two schedules: increasing batch size with constant learning rate (Theorem 2.3), and constant batch size with decaying learning rate (cosine annealing or linear; Theorem 2.4). The proofs proceed by bounding the norm of the 'search direction noise' between GSAM and gradient descent (Theorems 2.1 and 2.2). Numerical experiments train ResNets and ViT-Tiny on CIFAR-100 and measure flatness of converged minima.
key_results: GSAM with doubly increasing batch size or cosine-annealing learning rate finds flatter local minima than GSAM with constant batch size and constant learning rate on CIFAR-100 with ResNets and ViT-Tiny.
The search direction noise norm E[eta_t * ||omega_t||] is monotonically decreasing in batch size b_t, confirming that larger batch sizes reduce stochasticity in GSAM's update direction.
Convergence rate for GSAM with increasing batch (result 7) and decaying LR (result 8): E[||grad f_SAM*||] <= epsilon, matching or improving on prior SAM convergence results.
limitations: Limited number of models and datasets used in experiments (ResNet and ViT-Tiny on CIFAR-100 only).
Analysis focuses on GSAM rather than vanilla SAM; convergence guarantees are for the approximated SAM problem (gradient-norm surrogate), not the original minimax.
Flatness comparison is observational and does not establish that flatter minima found by these schedules lead to better generalization.
relevance_to_rq: Peripheral relevance: this paper studies SAM convergence theory and training schedules for finding flat minima, tangentially related to the flatness_theory and sam_origin sub-topics. It does not address OOD generalization or representation stability, so it does not directly inform the core RQ.
